note: OpenFEMA NfipClaims v3, state eq 'PR', 25387 claim records, data as of 2026-09-08. Island total: 25387 claims since 1978, 18592 with a payment, $161,097,734 paid (building $75,998,810, contents $85,098,924, increased cost of compliance $0); nominal dollars, not adjusted for inflation. Summed: amountPaidOnBuildingClaim + amountPaidOnContentsClaim + amountPaidOnIncreasedCostOfComplianceClaim, gross of later recoveries; 6703 records carry no amounts and count as claims with $0 paid; records with a negative amount (FEMA: a reissued check), summed as given: 1. nfip_claims_paid = claims whose three amounts sum to more than zero. Municipio = first five digits of censusGeoid (FEMA's block-group code), else countyCode (1044 records). 3966 claims ($14,769,930) have neither, or a code outside Puerto Rico, and are in no municipio (3448 of them with a loss before 2000): municipio values are a floor. FEMA redacts the address, so nothing finer than a block group is known. Hurricane María = floodEvent names Maria: 712 claims, $27,773,783 paid, of which 35 claims ($760,749) have no municipio. 704 of them have a date of loss in September 2017; September 2017 holds 713 claims in all, the rest being Hurricane Irma 6, no event name 3, which are not counted as María. Tract values use the first eleven digits of censusGeoid and only tracts that exist in the current TIGER set (658 tracts); 1281 located claims carry a tract code that is not current and appear at municipio level only. A claim is one policyholder's filing: not a count of flooded homes, since homes without a policy file nothing.
